attachments.origin_landmark: inner surface of the thyroid cartilage lamina (the laryngeal cartilages are not modeled as skeletal elements in this pass -- approximated via the adjacent hyoid attachment region)
attachments.insertion_landmark: anterolateral surface of the arytenoid cartilage

actions: shortens and relaxes the vocal folds
its superior fibres (thyroepiglottic part) widen the laryngeal inlet

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Antagonist to cricothyroid: it slackens the fold that cricothyroid tenses. Pitch is set by the balance between them.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Percutaneous EMG-guided injection through the cricothyroid membrane (Blitzer technique), not ultrasound: with the neck extended, a hollow monopolar EMG needle is inserted through the skin in the midline over the cricothyroid membrane, then angled roughly 20-30 degrees off midline and directed posterosuperiorly and laterally so the tip passes through the membrane and lies within the body of the thyroarytenoid muscle, just deep to the thyroid cartilage lamina; both sides are injected in the same setting for adductor spasmodic dysphonia. A supraglottic alternative (through the false-fold/aryepiglottic tissue rather than through the membrane) has also been described, sparing direct vocal-fold trauma.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to the cricothyroid membrane, within the paraglottic space at the level of the true vocal fold; in the supraglottic approach the injectate travels from the false fold a mean 12.9mm (SD 1.7mm) to reach the TA muscle complex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG activity that increases sharply with phonation (sustained /i/ or /e/) and during a Valsalva-type adduction maneuver confirms the needle tip is within TA rather than in paraglottic fat or cricothyroid muscle.
structures_at_risk: lateral cricoarytenoid muscle, immediately deep/inferior to TA -- diffusion occurs in most injections (reported in up to 94% of cadaver specimens) and is thought to contribute to the intended adductor effect rather than being a complication
cricothyroid muscle -- diffusion reported in roughly 40% of specimens, a candidate explanation for post-injection pitch change

posterior cricoarytenoid muscle -- diffusion is uncommon (under 10% of specimens) but is the presumed mechanism of the rare, occasionally bilateral abductor paralysis/stridor complication of TA injection
airway lumen/vocal fold mucosa, if the needle is advanced too far medially
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: This is the standard treatment for adductor spasmodic dysphonia and one of the oldest, best-documented indications for botulinum toxin of any muscle group. Guidance is by percutaneous EMG, never ultrasound.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Blitzer A, Brin MF, Stewart CF, 'Botulinum toxin management of spasmodic dysphonia (laryngeal dystonia): a 12-year experience in more than 900 patients', Laryngoscope 108(10):1435-1441 (1998), doi:10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003 (https://doi.org/10.1097/00005537-199810000-00003) -- retrieved via PubMed; Alonso VM, Chagury AA, Hachiya A, Imamura R, Tsuji DH, Sennes LU, 'Diffusion of aniline blue injected into the thyroarytenoid muscle as a proxy for botulinum toxin injection: an experimental study in cadaver larynges', Int Arch Otorhinolaryngol 17(3):315-320 (2013), doi:10.7162/S1809-977720130003000012 (https://doi.org/10.7162/S1809-977720130003000012) -- 18 cadaver larynges, PMC4423331; Lee HJ, Kim IB, Kim BH, Lee JH, 'Analysis of Dye Distribution in Cadaveric Supraglottic Injections: Elucidating the Mechanism of Action for Supraglottic Botulinum Neurotoxin Injection', J Voice (2026), doi:10.1016/j.jvoice.2026.04.016 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jvoice.2026.04.016) -- 13 cadavers, supraglottic approach -- all retrieved via PubMed
